title: Interpretation of Curriculum Design
text:
INTERPRETATION OF THE
 CURRICULUM DESIGNS
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A SYLLABUS AND A
CURRICULUM DESIGN
 A syllabus is a concise written guideline on a specific
 learning or subject area of the curriculum
 It outlines and provides the objectives, the content time
 allocation and resources to be used during the execution of
 the lesson.
 A curriculum design is a detailed outline of what is to be
 covered in a specific learning area.
 It prescribes how learning outcomes will be actualized through
 suggested learning experiences, key inquiry questions and
 learning resources.
 It provides the teacher with suggested criterion referenced
 assessment rubrics in every sub-strand.

ESSENCE STATEMENT
 An essence statement gives a general overview of a learning
 area. It summarizes the fundamental ideas of each learning
 area. It also explains the rationale and justification of
 inclusion of the learning area in the curriculum.
STRAND AND SUB-STRAND
 A strand is a broad area of study within a specific learning
 area. It is a consistent phenomenological idea or concept,
 that runs through the learning area.
 A strand also cuts across all levels of education.
 A sub-strand represents smaller concepts within the strand

 Assessment
 Assessment in CBC can be done through the following
 methods:
 Observation
 Written assignment
 Oral questions
It should be noted that in CBC, there should no ranking of
learners. Learner’s competencies should be assessed at an
individual’s level.
It should also be noted that assessment rubric for a
specific learning outcome should be developed for each
learner.
